4 ارتم , inf. n. إِرْتَامٌ, [app. He tied a رَتِيمَة, q. v.]. (T.) رَتْمٌ, also, as an inf. n., [i. e. of ↓ رَتَمَ ,] signifies The tying a thread, or string, upon one's own finger for the purpose of remembering something. (KL.) ―
-b2- And ارتمهُ, (inf. n. as above, S,) He tied upon his (a man's, T, S, Mgh) finger a thread, or string, such as is termed رَتِيمَة. (T, S, M, Mgh, K.) ＝
-A2- Also He (a young camel) bore fat in his hump. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
